project.description_en: At the end of the theme, the child shows a corner of the classroom made with the group, says the names of two classmates and the teacher, greets in English and in French, and shows one school rule.

activities.goal_en: Listen to a short story and say how the character feels.
activities.prompt_en: Listen to the story of Tani. How does Tani feel in the morning? And at the end of the day?
steps_en: Show the picture of a school and ask what happens there.
Tell the story slowly, with your hands and your face.
Ask: How did Tani feel? Who helped her?
Let the child tell the story again with you.
observe_en: Listens until the end of the story.
Says one feeling of the character (sad, afraid, happy).
Names who helped Tani.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 14 (Storytelling: Short stories), p. 39; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.story_en: On her first day at school, Tani held her mother’s hand very tight. The classroom was big and noisy. Tani wanted to cry. Then a girl with red ribbons came and said: “Hello! I am Ewi. Do you want to play with the blocks?” Tani built a tall tower with Ewi. When her mother came back, Tani said: “Mummy, tomorrow I am coming back to play with Ewi!”

activities.goal_en: Recognise one’s own name written on a card.
activities.prompt_en: Here are some name cards. Can you find the card with your name?
steps_en: Write the child’s name on a card in clear lowercase letters, with a capital first letter.
Read it aloud, pointing to each letter from left to right.
Mix it with two other name cards.
Ask the child to find their card, then to put it on their peg or chair.
observe_en: Finds their own name card among three.
Says the first letter of their name.
Follows the letters from left to right with a finger.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 17 (Reading: Listening and reading words), p. 42; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Hold the crayon correctly and draw vertical lines from top to bottom.
activities.prompt_en: The rain falls from the sky to the ground. Draw the rain: from the top, down!
steps_en: Show how to hold the crayon between the thumb and two fingers.
Draw a line in the air from top to bottom, saying “down”.
Draw lines in sand or on a slate.
Draw lines on paper, from the top line to the bottom line.
observe_en: Holds the crayon with three fingers.
Starts each line at the top.
Draws lines that go down without stopping.
materials_en: a sand tray or a slate
source_refs: Nursery One, table 18 (Writing: Pre-letter formation), p. 43; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Greet the teacher and friends in French in the morning.
activities.prompt_en: In French, we say “Bonjour !” in the morning. Say “Bonjour, Madame !” to your teacher.
steps_en: Say “Bonjour !” with a smile and a wave.
The child repeats “Bonjour !”.
Practise “Bonjour, Madame !” and “Bonjour, Monsieur !”.
Greet a puppet, then a real person.
observe_en: Says “Bonjour” clearly.
Uses “Madame” or “Monsieur”.
Greets with a smile and looks at the person.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 19 (French: Salutations), p. 44; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Count objects from 1 to 5 and say how many there are.
activities.prompt_en: How many crayons are in the box? Let us touch each one and count.
steps_en: Put 3 to 5 crayons on the table.
Touch each crayon and say one number: one, two, three…
Say the last number again: “There are four crayons.”
Change the number of crayons and count again.
observe_en: Touches one object for each number.
Says the numbers in order up to 5.
Repeats the last number to say how many.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 20 (Mathematics: Counting), p. 45; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

interactive.prompt_en: How many crayons can you see?
interactive.explanation_en: Touch each crayon: one, two, three, four. There are 4 crayons.

activities.title_en: Red, blue, yellow: sorting our things
activities.prompt_en: Put all the red things here, the blue things there and the yellow things here.
steps_en: Show three baskets with a red, a blue and a yellow paper.
Name the colour of one object and put it in the right basket.
Give the child objects one by one to sort.
Count the objects in each basket together.
observe_en: Names the three colours.
Puts each object in the basket of its colour.
Says which basket has the most.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 20 (Mathematics: Classifying elements), p. 45; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Hear the difference between a soft voice and a loud voice and choose the right one.
activities.prompt_en: Listen: is my voice soft or loud? In the classroom, we use a soft voice.
steps_en: Say a word softly, then loudly.
The child shows a small hand for soft and a big hand for loud.
Ask: where do we use a soft voice? (classroom, a baby sleeping)
Play: whisper a word, the child repeats it softly.
observe_en: Hears the difference between soft and loud.
Uses a soft voice when asked.
Gives one place where we speak softly.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 21 (Sensory and Perceptive Education: The sense of hearing), p. 46; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: My name, my teacher, my school
activities.goal_en: Introduce oneself and name the teacher and the school.
activities.prompt_en: Tell me: what is your name? What is your teacher’s name? What is the name of your school?
steps_en: Introduce yourself first: “My name is…”.
The child says “My name is…”.
Show the teacher and say their name together.
Walk to the school gate or sign and read the school name.
observe_en: Says “My name is…” clearly.
Names the teacher.
Recognises the school name or sign.
materials_en: a photo of the class or the school sign
source_refs: Nursery One, table 24 (Citizenship: Self-introduction), p. 50; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Follow simple safety rules in the playground and tell the teacher when something happens.
activities.prompt_en: In the playground, we wait our turn on the slide, we do not push and we tell the teacher if someone is hurt.
steps_en: Walk round the playground and point to the swings, the slide or the open space.
Say one rule for each place.
Act: one child falls; another runs to tell the teacher.
Repeat the rules with gestures.
observe_en: Waits for their turn.
Says one rule (do not push, wait your turn).
Knows to tell the teacher.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 27 (Safety Education: School safety), p. 53; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Washing my hands step by step
activities.goal_en: Wash hands with soap and water in the right order.
activities.prompt_en: Before eating and after the toilet, we wash our hands: water, soap, rub, rinse, dry.
steps_en: Wet the hands with clean water.
Put soap and rub the palms, the backs and between the fingers.
Rinse with clean water.
Dry with a clean towel or in the air.
observe_en: Uses soap.
Rubs between the fingers.
Rinses and dries the hands.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 28 (Health Education and Nutrition: Good health habits), p. 54; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Doh, reh, mih: climbing the stairs
activities.goal_en: Use the voice to make the sounds doh, reh, mih going up.
activities.prompt_en: Our voice can climb stairs: doh, reh, mih! And come down: mih, reh, doh!
steps_en: Show three steps with your hand at three heights.
Sing “doh” low, “reh” a little higher, “mih” higher.
The child sings and moves the hand with you.
Sing up and down slowly, then a little faster.
observe_en: Sings the three sounds.
Moves the hand up and down with the voice.
Enjoys singing with the group.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 29 (Music and Dance: Sol-fa notations), p. 55; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Walking and running in a line
activities.goal_en: Walk and run in a line, starting and stopping on a signal.
activities.prompt_en: When I clap once, walk. When I clap twice, run. When I raise my hand, stop!
steps_en: Make a line of children, one behind the other.
Clap once: everyone walks.
Clap twice: everyone runs slowly in the line.
Raise your hand: everyone stops and stands still.
observe_en: Stays in the line.
Changes from walking to running on the signal.
Stops on the signal.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 32 (Physical Education and Sports: Athletics), p. 58; theme 1: The school (table 13, p. 37)

scale.description: Succeeds mostly with a model or help.
Sometimes succeeds alone, sometimes with a reminder.
Succeeds on their own in a familiar situation.

indicators: Greets the teacher and classmates in English and says “Bonjour”.
Says their own name and the teacher’s name.
Washes hands in the right order.
Walks and runs in a line on a signal.

sources: Cameroon Nursery School Curriculum, English Subsystem, MINEDUB, 2018: table 13 (integrated learning themes), p. 37; Nursery One tables, cited and not reproduced.
